text:
sam: Quick summary — ran AWQ/GPTQ/FP8/INT8 bakeoff against the funcall suite (2.1k prompts) with our standard deployment profiles (hosted small-batch, dedicated high-throughput). Observed structured-output (JSON) correctness regressions only under AWQ/FP8 combo when KV cache + continuous batching enabled. Fail rate ~1.8% vs ~0.05% baseline on full-precision. Details below.

anya: Oof, that sounds like the same class of failures we saw last quarter but different trigger. Do you have minimal repro examples?

sam: Yup, here's a trimmed failing response (AWQ fp8, batch_size=16, cache enabled):

```
request: {"prompt":"call tool get_user({\"id\":123})"}
response: "{\"tool\": \"get_user\", \"args\": {\"id\": 123, \"include_profile\": true,,}}"
```

Note the double-comma after include_profile and trailing comma before closing brace — invalid JSON. On the same prompt GPTQ-int8 and FP32 return valid JSON.

liam: Do we know whether tokenization or temperature/bias changes are causing extra punctuation? Could be rounding of logits causing different arg delimiters.

sam: I ran a token-level diff. For failing cases AWQ's generation inserted an extra token for "," (0x2c) in places where FP32 produced a PAD or nothing due to slightly different argmax choices. The divergence correlates with the quantized kernel selected for that layer.

marta: Interesting. Which kernel path did the compiler pick? Any pattern by seq_len or batch?

sam: Yes — when seq_len > 512 and batch>=12, runtime picked the block-tiling kernel (path: tiled_attn_fast) for AWQ/FP8 builds. For GPTQ-int8 and FP32 it uses tiled_attn_stable. The failure rate spikes in the tiled_attn_fast path.

anya: Could this be a mismatch in attention softmax numeric stability leading to a stray punctuation token? If tiled_attn_fast is less stable under quantization that makes sense.

sam: That's our hypothesis. Quick experiment: forced runtime to use tiled_attn_stable for AWQ/FP8 (env override) and reran 1k samples — failure drops to 0.06%. So it's deterministic to kernel choice.

liam: Nice isolate. Does disabling KV cache reproduce the drop?

sam: Disabling cache also reduces failures (to ~0.2%) but less effective than forcing stable kernel. So it's an interaction: cache + tiled_attn_fast + batch shaping seems to push logits into a quantization-sensitive regime.

marta: Any perf tradeoff if we force stable kernel on Dedicated?

sam: Measured 8-12% throughput loss on Dedicated p4-equivalent for long sequences. On hosted small-batch the perf hit is ~3-4% because we were already small-batch limited.

anya: So short term: revert kernel selection for AWQ/FP8 on rollout (canary only), add a regression test in funcall suite that exercises the tiled_attn_fast path, and gate AWQ/FP8 on that. Long term: fix numerical stability in tiled_attn_fast or add quantization-aware calibration.

sam: That's the proposed plan. I'll open a PR to add the regression (tests/funcall/quant_kernel_smoke) + a config to force stable kernel for AWQ/FP8 canaries.

infra-bot: note: Created issue INF-2314 "AWQ FP8 tiled_attn_fast -> JSON emission drift" and scheduled a canary rollback workflow template.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout (AWQ FP8) to dev-dedicated on 2026-05-02 18:30 UTC, will use kernel override stable=true.

liam: For the regression test, can you include a tiny corpus with different seq_len/batch combos and the exact failing pattern? Also capture token logits around the comma token so we can compare quantized vs float at the logit level.

sam: Yep — will include 8 prompts that triggered the failure + a small harness to dump logits for the punctuation tokens. PR after lunch.

marta: Also add an eval threshold in the CI that fails the model onboarding if structured-output failure > 0.3% for the funcall suite. That prevents accidental regressions in future quant builds.

sam: Agreed. I'll update the onboarding checklist and notify ML onboarding channel when PR is up.

anya: Thanks. This is great isolation — one actionable kernel switch with perf tradeoffs.

sam: TL;DR: AWQ+FP8 + tiled_attn_fast + KV cache -> small but real JSON emission drift. Mitigation: force stable kernel for canary, add regression, and track in INF-2314.
